learning_objective: 🎯 Demystify the internet! Understand how computers talk to each other across the globe, the hardware that connects them, and how websites actually work.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Networks are classified by size. LAN (Local) is inside one building/school. MAN (Metropolitan) covers a city (like cable TV). WAN (Wide) connects countries/continents—the Internet is the ultimate WAN!

The physical layout of computers. Star (all connected to a central hub), Bus (all on one single main cable), Ring (connected in a circle), Tree (hierarchical), and Mesh (every computer connected to every other computer).

A Hub simply broadcasts data to everyone. A Switch is 'smart' and sends data ONLY to the specific target computer. A Router connects different networks (like your home Wi-Fi to your ISP). A Modem converts digital signals to analog and back.
Protocols are strict rules for communication. TCP/IP breaks data into packets and routes them. HTTP/HTTPS is used for transferring web pages safely. FTP is specifically for transferring files.

The WWW is a collection of linked documents. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the web address. A Web Browser is the client software that asks for a page, and a Web Server is the massive computer that stores the page (Web Hosting) and sends it back.

fun_activity.title: 📡 The Packet Router Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine sending an image on WhatsApp. TCP chops the image into 100 tiny digital puzzle pieces (packets). IP stamps the destination address on each one. They all take different routes across the internet and are perfectly reassembled on your friend's phone!

exam_tips: 📌 Full forms are guaranteed 1-mark questions: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), URL (Uniform Resource Locator), ISP (Internet Service Provider), MAC (Media Access Control).
📌 Star topology is the most commonly used in schools/labs because if one wire breaks, only that single computer fails. In a Bus topology, if the main wire breaks, the whole network crashes.
📌 Know the difference between the Internet (the physical infrastructure of cables and routers) and the WWW (the software/pages that run on top of the internet).
quick_recap: ⭐ A switch is much more secure and efficient than a hub because it reduces network traffic.
⭐ HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP; the 'S' means the data is encrypted, making it safe for passwords and banking.
⭐ Every device on a network must have a unique IP address to send and receive data.
